# `proj version get`

Get the project version based on the `VERSION` file.

## Standard Behavior

Select a project with `--project PATH`, or let the command find the nearest
recognized project folder. It reads VERSION and prints a version such as `v1.0.0`.
VERSION can contain plain version text or the supported JSON object.

If the `VERSION` file is missing, the tool attempts to fall back and parse the version from an R package `DESCRIPTION` file if one is present in the project root. If neither a `VERSION` file nor a `DESCRIPTION` file exists, it reports `v0.0.1` without creating a file.
Reading a version does not synchronize VERSION and DESCRIPTION. That proposed
synchronization remains in an unmerged change.

```bash
proj version get
```

## Options

### `--no-v`

Omits the 'v' prefix from the output string.

```bash
proj version get --no-v
```

### `--format <FORMAT>`

Specifies the output format:

- `text` (default): Outputs the version as a standard string identifier.
- `json`: Outputs the version as a serialized JSON object, detailing its properties (`major`, `minor`, `patch`, and optionally `dev`).

```bash
proj version get --format json
```

## JSON Output Properties

When using `--format=json`, the output consists of the separated standard semantic components:

- `major` (integer)
- `minor` (integer)
- `patch` (integer)
- `dev` (integer, optional, indicating build cycles or pre-release versioning)


## Existing DESCRIPTION metadata

In this source candidate, VERSION writes also synchronize the Version field of an
existing DESCRIPTION by default. No DESCRIPTION is created. Disable with
settings.sync-description-version: false. See the [policy and preservation limits](../configuration.qmd#version-and-description-synchronization-source-candidate).
